sources.entry: PureSnitch - Open-source application firewall with a Little Snitch-style world map, rule manager, DNS over HTTPS, and pf-based blocking, with no telemetry. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/momenbasel/puresnitch) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: PureSnitch is a free, open-source, MIT-licensed application firewall and connection monitor for macOS, styled after Little Snitch, with host-wide pf-based IP/CIDR/port blocking and an experimental manual DNS-over-HTTPS proxy.
keywords: see what my mac is connecting to
summary.what_it_does: PureSnitch shows live network connections per process in a Network Monitor window, with a per-process bandwidth sidebar and host lists for each process. A Rules Manager lists, searches, enables, disables and deletes rules, plus blocklist and rule group sections. Blocklists (1Hosts, OISD, StevenBlack, HaGeZi) are built in and refresh when the helper starts or on request. Enforcement is opt-in and loads deny-only, host-wide IPv4/CIDR/port rules into a runtime pf anchor, and can run an experimental loopback DNS proxy that forwards to a DoH upstream (Cloudflare, Quad9, Google or custom) for clients configured manually. A privileged helper, installed via SMAppService, handles the root-level work over XPC. The README states the app does not perform per-process kernel filtering, does not change system DNS, and collects no telemetry.
use_cases: see which apps on my Mac are making network connections
block outbound connections to specific IPs or ranges
block ads and trackers with domain blocklists on macOS
replace a paid Little Snitch license
experiment with a local DNS-over-HTTPS proxy
audit an open-source firewall for macOS
how_to_run: Or download the signed .dmg from Releases and drag PureSnitch into /Applications

Build from source: brew install xcodegen; xcodegen generate; xcodebuild -project PureSnitch.xcodeproj -scheme PureSnitch -configuration Release -derivedDataPath build CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="-" CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build
notable: Little Snitch-style UI: menubar status item, world map, rules manager and connection alert popups
Host-wide deny-only pf rules in a runtime com.apple/puresnitch anchor, with enforcement off by default
Built-in blocklist library (1Hosts, OISD, StevenBlack, HaGeZi) that refreshes on helper start
Signed, notarized release DMG and Homebrew cask; universal binary from v0.2.0 with macOS 13+ minimum
Explicit no-telemetry stance; network access limited to blocklist refreshes and opt-in DNS proxy traffic
caveats: No per-process kernel filtering in the shipping build; it requires Apple's Network Extension entitlement, which the README says is not yet granted (NetExt is dormant)
DNS proxy is experimental, loopback-only, and applies only to clients manually configured to use it; it does not replace the system resolver
Only the Default profile is enforced; other profiles are labels, and SSID-based switching is not implemented

Requires installing a privileged helper and approving it in System Settings; must be installed in /Applications; the README says a certificate-free source build cannot run live monitoring or enforcement
